ev.q: pregnant women were significantly more likely than were nonpregnant women to be admitted to an intensive care unit
Among symptomatic women, 23,434 (5.7%) were reported to be pregnant.
Compared with nonpregnant women, pregnant women more frequently were admitted to an ICU
Stratifying these analyses by age and race/ethnicity highlighted disparities in risk by subgroup.
This analysis included cases initially reported to CDC during January 22–October 3, 2020

methods_quotes.q: Crude and adjusted RRs and 95% CIs were calculated using modified Poisson regression.
Overall and stratified risk ratios were adjusted for age (in years), race/ethnicity, and presence of diabetes, cardiovascular disease (including hypertension), and chronic lung disease.
Outcomes with missing data were assumed not to have occurred.
Crude and adjusted risk ratios were not calculated for cell sizes <5.
